title: How the Piano Was Invented
meta_description: Meet Bartolomeo Cristofori, the maker who developed the piano’s hammer action, and learn how the instrument evolved from earlier keyboard designs.
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: Bartolomeo Cristofori, an Italian instrument maker working for the Medici court in Florence, developed the piano around 1700.
The crucial innovation was a hammer mechanism that strikes a string and then escapes from it, allowing the string to vibrate freely and the player to vary loudness by touch.
Earlier keyboard instruments such as the harpsichord plucked strings, making dynamic control through key pressure much more limited.
A Cristofori piano dated 1720 survives in The Metropolitan Museum of Art; early pianos had fewer keys and a different tone and action from modern concert grands.
